Taalas, an AI chip startup developing
specialised hardware for artificial intelligence models, has been acquired by
AMD in a deal valued at approximately $2.9 billion. The transaction also
highlights the growing role of European engineering talent and venture capital
in the global AI hardware industry.

Founded in Toronto in 2023 by Serbian
engineer Ljubiša Bajić, alongside Lejla Bajić and Drago Ignjatović, Taalas
develops specialised chips that integrate AI models directly into silicon. The
company raised approximately $220 million from investors including Quiet
Capital, Lamond Ventures, Fidelity and Belgrade-based Fifth Quarter Ventures
(5QV).

Taalas takes a different approach to AI
computing by designing chips around specific AI models rather than relying on
general-purpose GPUs. Its first demonstrator chip, developed for Meta's Llama
3.1 8B model, reportedly achieves around 17,000 tokens per second per user. AMD
plans to incorporate the technology into its Instinct accelerator roadmap.

The acquisition also marks the second
unicorn founded by Ljubiša Bajić, who previously co-founded AI chip company
Tenstorrent, valued at $6.2 billion. Tenstorrent operates an R&D office in
Belgrade, reflecting Serbia's growing presence in the AI hardware and
semiconductor industry. Several international technology companies have
established research and development operations in the country, contributing to
advances in AI computing, chip design and related technologies.

Commenting on the acquisition, Tihomir Bajić, General Partner at Fifth Quarter Ventures, said:

Taalas is a reminder that some of the
most important work in AI is happening below the model, in the chips and
systems that make it run. When we started Fund I, betting on AI compute from
Belgrade sounded esoteric. Today, it proves to be the right call.

Europe doesn't have to watch the AI
hardware race from the sidelines. The talent is already here, in Belgrade,
building chips for the world's biggest companies. Backing these founders before
consensus helped us win already, and we intend to do much more of it.

Taalas was among the early investments
made by Fifth Quarter Ventures through its first fund. The Belgrade-based
venture capital firm focuses on supporting technology startups and founders
from the Adriatic region and its diaspora, particularly in deeptech and
AI-related sectors.
